A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on neural collapse, batch normalization, and weight decay. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including the earlier real-world results grid retained on v3's final PDF page.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments with synthetic datasets and MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, using MLP, VGG, and ResNet models in Section 3 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 reports original weight-decay experiments, training-loss trajectories, controlled feature-norm experiments, and ImageNet32 results in Section 3 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The work retains its analysis of existing BN and WD in layer-peeled cross-entropy classifiers without proposing a new learning or inference algorithm. Changes to experimental network configurations and cosine-similarity measurements concern evaluation settings and mathematical definitions.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluated ImageNet32 coverage with 1000 classes, substantially extending the classification setting. Conic-hull and MLP3-generated data remain, but v1's MLP6-generated dataset results are absent. MNIST and the earlier CIFAR coverage remain represented in the retained real-world grid on v3's final page.

E2.justification: The principal comparison families remain MLP/VGG with and without BN and ResNet with BN. However, v1 explicitly modifies BN-VGG by replacing dropout with BN, while v3 specifies official PyTorch implementations for its new comparisons, revising the documented comparator variant. The earlier VGG/ResNet comparison also survives on v3's final page.

E3.justification: v3 reports Adam training for 300 epochs, replacing the SGD and 100–200-epoch settings reported in v1. Synthetic experiments change from 3/6/9-layer models with BN between adjacent layers to 4/6-layer models with a single final-feature BN layer. WD sweeps change, cosine definitions explicitly subtract the global feature mean, and average-class measurements accompany worst-class measurements. These are reported protocol changes, not evidence of same-setting performance gains.

E4.justification: Sections 3.3–3.4 and Appendices B.3–B.4 add training-loss/NC trajectories and interventions fixing the BN scale vector to investigate feature norms across WD settings. These directly examine training dynamics and the proposed norm mechanism beyond v1's WD, BN, and model-depth comparisons.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly specifies five random-seed runs for synthetic experiments and three for real-world experiments. v3 retains five-experiment standard deviations in Figure 2 and specifies three for the feature-norm experiment in Figure 4, but omits equivalent seed and repetition disclosures for its new real-world comparisons. Standard deviation remains the main uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds findings on BN-dependent loss/NC trajectories, generally weaker NC at larger fixed feature norms, and ImageNet32 results where VGG inter-class similarity increases with WD despite stronger intra-class collapse. Its synthetic and CIFAR plots also contain newly reported curves under revised settings. These are additional or replaced results, not directly comparable performance improvements; the earlier real-world grid is retained.

T1.justification: The advertised WD-dependent error factor changes from exp(O(C/lambda)) to (C/lambda)^O(C). v3 revises the centered cosine definitions, supplies a new Holder-based normalization-lemma proof, adds a Proposition C.1/Markov derivation, and removes formal Conjecture 3.1. NC3 bounds become explicit in theorem statements, although a weight–feature alignment bound already appeared in v1's Appendix A.3.

C1.justification: The central BN/WD explanation remains, but v3 substantially strengthens the advertised dependence of its principal guarantee on WD. It also withdraws v1's positioning of cosine similarity as a newly proposed measure and emphasizes near-optimal, worst-class guarantees and understanding established training techniques.

C2.justification: v3 interprets training trajectories and controlled feature-norm experiments, explains the saturated six-layer conic-hull case, and attributes ImageNet32 exceptions to optimization becoming more influential with many classes. It adds limitations concerning biases and BN/activation ordering. However, Section 3.4 and Figure 9 contain statements favoring higher feature norms that contradict the predominant plotted trend and abstract.

D1.justification: The experimental recipes are substantially revised: v3 documents Adam/300 epochs, RTX4090 hardware, official PyTorch models, synthetic dimension 16, ImageNet32's 100,000 samples and learning rate, and fixed-gamma interventions. v1 instead documents SGD budgets, Colab and TITAN RTX/2080 Ti hardware, batch size 128, and Han et al. demo-code provenance. Some earlier implementation disclosures disappear.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning through dedicated WD and BN literature discussions and Appendix A's theoretical comparison table. It adds work on optimization, normalization, and deeper neural collapse, and attributes cosine-similarity measurement to Kornblith et al. rather than presenting that measurement as its own invention.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contributions, related work, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. Experiments are reorganized around BN/WD, training loss, and feature norm instead of principally separating synthetic and real-world datasets. The appendices become theoretical comparisons, experiments, and proofs, with substantial explanatory restructuring.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the conic-hull illustration with an NC visualization, adds a theoretical comparison table, rebuilds plots to juxtapose average and worst-class measurements, and adds loss-trajectory and feature-norm panels. Real-world results move predominantly to the appendix; the earlier full grid remains as an uncaptioned final page.

improvement.justification: v3 provides substantially broader empirical evidence and replaces an unsupported normalization-proof step with a detailed Holder derivation. However, its newly added Proposition C.1 is false as stated: with N=2, a=(1,0), and b=(2,1), it requires 1/2 >= 2/3. This undermines the added derivation on PDF pages 28–29. Contradictory feature-norm explanations further weaken reporting reliability. These substantive benefits and mathematical/reporting defects leave the net quality uncertain.
